project.name: Site Delivery Check
project.problem: Freelance web developers manually compare a finished page with a client brief and lack a compact record of exactly what was checked.
project.user: An independent web developer preparing a small business landing page for client delivery from their own local build.
project.outcome: A reviewed checklist tied to brief quotes and actual browser measurements; reduced preparation effort is a hypothesis to measure.
project.overlayDecision: Briefs and exported evidence may contain client text, so privacy applies. UI and English/Roman Urdu input trigger interface/i18n. Draft latency and browser resource bounds trigger performance. npm, model and runtime trigger dependencies/licensing/distribution. Browser and model jobs trigger concurrency and local operation. Public developer-facing source/demo triggers release review. No billing, auth, financial execution, model training, hosted service, behavioral telemetry, regulated-sector claim, migration or continuity promise is planned.
project.initialUserCountry: Pakistan for any voluntarily recruited tester; broader distribution unknown.
project.dataPolicy: Synthetic demos, client-authorized brief text only, no stored client histories, no remote inference. Reports persist only through explicit local export.
project.commercialHypothesis: Freelancers might pay for local setup/support or the time saved before delivery. No price, revenue or willingness-to-pay claim is verified.

model.integrity: SHA-256 verified against the local manifest on 14 October 2026. Task performance remains untested.

repositorySearch.capability: Local brief-to-reviewable check mapping, bounded page inspection, and evidence reports without generated-code execution.
repositorySearch.summary: Adopt the official browser and already downloaded runtime; inspect one exact test-generation comparator. No application repository removes the need for our small review/report workflow. Search results do not establish novelty.

claims.text: Week 2 requires a new open-AI project, published DEV entry, demo and repository before 18 October 23:59 PDT.
ScopeCraft's published description substantially overlaps our original generic brief-to-proposal suggestion.
Playwright 1.63.0's official manifest specifies Chromium revision 1243, matching the preserved directory.
All five exact proposed package reports completed with no direct advisory records and no dependency-graph errors; this is not a resolved-lockfile scan.
The upstream Qwen3 1.7B card declares Apache-2.0; task accuracy and Roman Urdu quality are unproven.
The reviewed report may reduce checklist preparation and clarify website delivery discussions.
The preserved small model may reliably classify supported requirements with exact source quotes within the latency budget.
Preserved model content matches its local manifest digest, and the browser binary version matches the selected Playwright browser manifest. This establishes integrity/version fit, not task accuracy.

decisions.text: User delegated the refinement choice; select brief-to-website delivery checks and use the chosen site-delivery-check folder.
Qwen proposes quote-grounded data; reviewed parameters drive fixed browser checks. Never execute model-written code or treat its verdict as measurement.
Initial scope is one developer-controlled local HTTP page on a selected 127.0.0.1 port, fresh browser sessions, bounded reads, two viewports and explicit incomplete-resource notices.
Target the overall challenge; enter no partner category without meaningful implemented use.
Execute six reviewed tasks in this session; awaiting user review of the written implementation plan.
